label: Obstacle-Avoiding Robot
description: A mobile robot that senses obstacles and changes its movement to avoid collisions. This overview connects the main hardware, sensing principle, and control decisions.

label: Arduino
description: The microcontroller board runs the program, reads sensor signals, and sends control signals to the motor driver. Exact pin mappings depend on the board and wiring.

label: Ultrasonic sensor
description: The sensor estimates distance by sending an ultrasonic pulse and measuring how long its echo takes to return. Actual behavior depends on the sensor model and environment.

label: Control logic
description: The program compares measured distance with a threshold, then decides whether the robot should continue, stop, or turn. The threshold and movement strategy are design choices.

label: Board & pins
description: The board provides digital pins, power connections, and a microcontroller. Check the exact board revision before using pin numbers or voltage limits.

label: Program flow
description: A typical sketch repeatedly reads the sensor, calculates distance, evaluates a condition, and updates motor outputs. Timing and library details vary by implementation.

label: I/O signals
description: Input/output signals connect the controller to sensor and motor-driver modules. Signal voltage and pin compatibility should be checked for the selected hardware.

label: Echo timing
description: The time between sending a pulse and receiving its echo is used to estimate the round-trip travel time of sound.

label: Distance formula
description: Approximate distance = speed of sound × echo time ÷ 2. The division by two accounts for the sound travelling to the obstacle and back.

label: Accuracy limits
description: Readings can be affected by target angle, soft surfaces, temperature, sensor dead zones, and electrical noise. Validate with the actual hardware.

label: Threshold
description: A distance threshold is the point at which the robot changes behavior. Choose it based on speed, braking distance, sensor noise, and robot size.

label: Move / turn
description: The control logic translates a decision into motor-driver commands. The exact action depends on motor wiring, driver configuration, and the chosen avoidance strategy.
